headline: Nvidia Carries AI Worries Into a Holiday-Thinned Half Day
body_html:
Nvidia is the stock the whole market is talking about as traders return from the holiday. The chip giant fell 3.91% in Wednesday's session, the last before Thursday's closure. A prominent investor warned about the AI boom, and reports said the cost of insuring the debt of Nvidia, Oracle and Meta against default has surged.

Other headlines added to the pressure. Analysts are reassessing leadership and regulatory risks after the chief executive's reinstatement. Singapore has not confirmed whether advanced chip shipments were halted, and neocloud firms were reportedly told to choose between Nvidia chips and Chinese customers. Semiconductors fell 0.52% on average, with Lam Research down 5.68% and Micron down 4.57%. The S&P 500 slipped 0.29% and the Nasdaq lost 0.65%, yet 465 stocks rose against 195 that fell.

Overnight tone looks steadier. Reuters reports shares are finding footing after a bruising month, the dollar is set for a third monthly gain, and oil is on track to snap a three-week losing streak on supply fears. Today's session ends early, at 1:00 p.m. ET, so early moves may be thin. Watch whether chip stocks stabilize.

briefs.headline: Memory Names Sag on Forecast Cut
briefs.body: Micron fell 4.57% on Wednesday and Sandisk dropped 5.57% after TrendForce trimmed its 2027 memory forecasts. Commentary remains split on whether memory is nearing a peak. Huawei has also emerged as a fresh competitive worry for Micron.

briefs.headline: TSMC Gets an Upgrade Amid Policy Noise
briefs.body: TSMC slipped 1.96% on Wednesday even as it was upgraded to Strong Buy. Reports say it may make its Texas plant conditional, and that President Trump will attend a groundbreaking at its Arizona expansion. Both stories could shape the open.

briefs.headline: Cyclical Sectors Outran Tech
briefs.body: Energy led Wednesday's sector averages, up 2.12%, followed by materials at 1.85% and consumer staples at 1.27%. Industrials, consumer discretionary and financials each gained at least 1%. Healthcare slipped 0.17% and semiconductors lost 0.52%.

briefs.headline: Sharp Falls for Ambarella and Nutanix
briefs.body: Ambarella plunged 19.77% and Nutanix fell 15.19%, the steepest drops in the tracked universe. Urban Outfitters lost 10.33%. Traders will watch for follow-through or a bounce when the half-day session opens.

briefs.headline: Smaller Names Lead the Gainers
briefs.body: Innio rose 8.21% and SolarEdge gained 8.18%, while Semtech added 7.48%. Floor Decor climbed 7.07% and BlackLine rose 6.56%. The leaders spanned power equipment, solar, analog chips, retail and software.

briefs.headline: Gulf Tensions Keep Oil in Focus
briefs.body: Oil is on track to snap a three-week losing streak on supply fears. An attack on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery killed a worker and halted some operations. Reuters also reports the U.S. urged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC.
